title: FloodGuard Renewal Term Premium and the Renewal Rate Cap
content:
Rate manual clause — FloodGuard Private Flood Policy renewal term premium.

## Clause

The renewal term premium is the smaller of the indicated renewal premium on file and the capped premium, rounded half-up to the cent. The capped premium is the expiring term premium increased by the tier's renewal rate cap percentage, rounded half-up to the cent.

## Terms used

- Indicated renewal premium on file: the indicated premium for the upcoming term standing on the policy, excluding the policy fee.
- Expiring term premium: the annual term premium of the term now ending, excluding the policy fee.
- Capped premium: the expiring term premium increased by the tier's renewal rate cap percentage of itself, rounded half-up to the cent before it is compared.
- Credits on the renewal: every credit percentage rated on the renewal is added together, and the total reduces the smaller of the indicated renewal premium and the capped premium once; rounding half-up to the cent is applied only to that final renewal term premium. With no credit percentage rated, the renewal term premium is the smaller figure itself.

## Figures worked through (hypothetical)

The following cases use a hypothetical tier renewal rate cap percentage of 15.

| Expiring term premium | Capped premium | Indicated renewal premium on file | Smaller figure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 800.00 | 800.00 increased by 15 percent is 920.00 | 1,010.37 | 920.00 |
| 800.00 | 920.00 | 874.55 | 874.55 |
| 733.33 | 843.3295, rounded half-up to 843.33 | 900.00 | 843.33 |

With no credit percentage rated, each smaller figure is the renewal term premium.

With hypothetical credits totalling 5 percent, the 920.00 figure is reduced once by 5 percent to 874.00, and the 843.33 figure to 801.1635, rounded half-up at the end to 801.16. The credit percentages act once, as a single total, on the smaller figure; they are not applied one after another.
